newsitem.title: Italy: ALPINE SKIING-ERTL POISED FOR SURPRISE COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ERTL POISED FOR SURPRISE COMEBACK.

text.p: Germany's Martina Ertl could make a surprise comeback in Sunday's world championship giant slalom despite suffering a torn knee ligament last month.
A final decision about her participation would be taken fter a training run in Germany on Wednesday, German team spokesman Walter Vogel said on Tuesday.
Ertl, injured practising for the Cortina D'Ampezzo downhill on January 23, has trained with the men's team in Kleinwalsertal.
"She has no problems with her knee. She skied very well during the training," said Vogel.
German technical coach Wolfgang Maier said: "I believe Ertl will be able to race. She is very strong mentally."
At present she can ski only with a special brace to protect her knee.
German team doctor Ernst-Otto Muench said such a knee injury normally required a rest from five to six weeks.
"It is possible to ski with such a brace, but I don't think it is possible to deliver a 100 percent performance with such a thing," said Muench.
